ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, senior managers, and authorized representatives against Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, UN Security Council sanctions lists under the United Nations Act, Criminal Code Part II.1 listed terrorist entities, OFAC SDN List, and applicable EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists. Politically exposed persons, domestic and foreign, including heads of state, cabinet members, members of legislative bodies, senior judges, senior military officers, state enterprise executives, and political party leaders, together with family members and close associates, require enhanced due diligence, independent senior approval, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing monitoring. All KYC/UBO records must be retained for at least five years after the relationship ends, and any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing must be reported to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal - Registre des entreprises / Quebec Enterprise Registry, accessible via www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of a Quebec limited partnership must be in French and must contain the legal form indicator 'Societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' Alternatively, 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' may appear where authorized by OTTIAQ translation practice; however, the French version controls. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters and rendered phonetically in French; English versions are permitted only as secondary registered variants. The name may not contain numerals or symbols in a manner that is inconsistent with French usage.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Solidarity association terms requiring ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec issues written reasons. The applicant may file a corrected name reservation request online, addressing each reason stated. If a sensitive token was the basis for refusal, the applicant must first obtain the written authorization of the competent Quebec or federal minister and attach it to the reservation application. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may submit a written administrative review request to the Director of the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal. If administrative review fails, the decision may be challenged by way of judicial review before the Cour superieure du Quebec within 30 days. A reserved name may not be automatically extended; a fresh reservation must be filed after expiry or while the existing reservation is still active if the intended filing will not occur before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be accepted as the registered address for service of process and registry correspondence, provided the provider maintains a physical street address in Quebec and accepts legal documents during normal business hours. However, a virtual office alone will not establish commercial substance for income tax or GST/QST registration purposes. Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency may impute a permanent establishment or place of business to the actual management location, which is undesirable for the limited partner and may prejudice the intended pass-through tax treatment. For a digital advertising media-buying entity, a serviced office or fixed shared office with dedicated administrative capacity is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate for performance marketing and affiliate lead-generation intermediaries. Estimated 10-15% likelihood of an unannounced registered-office inspection within the first 18 months of operation, rising above 40% if any UBO is a politically exposed person, if cash-like payment rails are detected, if disproportionate affiliate commissions are paid to entities in high-risk jurisdictions, or if FINTRAC files a suspicious transaction report.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ), arts. 2187, 2236–2279 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ, c. P-44.1), ss. 2, 9, 17, 24; Charter of the French Language (RLRQ, c. C-11) for mandatory French name and signage.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), 2, Complexe Desjardins, C.P. 63, Montréal, QC H5B 1G3; online via the REQ business registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Statement of Registration) for a société en commandite; electronic filing via REQ e-service 'Immatriculer une entreprise'.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership; limited partners' liability is limited to their agreed contribution. Contributions may be cash or in-kind, and escrow is not mandated unless the limited partnership agreement so stipulates (none for digital media-buying). Non-resident ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Managing General Partner of [LP NAME], s.e.c. (i) subscribes to an initial capital contribution and hereby accepts the agreed contributions of each limited partner, as set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement dated [DATE]; (ii) adopts the registered office located at [REGISTERED OFFICE], Québec, and appoints the Registraire des entreprises as agent for service of process; (iii) appoints [GP] as Managing General Partner, [CCO] as Compliance Officer for AML/KYC and all media-buying contracts, and [CFO] as Chief Financial Officer, each with signing authority and power to open accounts; (iv) directs officers to file the Déclaration d'immatriculation with the Registraire des entreprises and to observe all publication, tax, and occupational health obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Jurisdiction name clearance and legal-form verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — business name search and reservation e-service; Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF) for French-language compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search and pre-validate the proposed name in the REQ public registry; ensure the name and legal-form suffix are in French, using 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; confirm the activity description aligns with NAICS 541810 / ISIC 7310; reserve the name online and retain the reservation receipt before preparing the declaration.
required_dossiers: Evidence of French-language compliance for commercial signage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or challenged, file a corrected name amendment through the REQ portal within 15 days and resubmit the reservation before the registration deadline; no registry penalty applies if corrected prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private law firm or notary engaged by the partners; no government filing is made at this substep.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the convention de société en commandite covering capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and general partner authority; confirm the eligibility of non-resident limited partners; have all partners execute the agreement; notarization is optional where no real property is acquired.
required_dossiers: Final limited partnership agreement (signed by all partners)
Identity and suitability documents for KYC of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later requests an extract, provide a certified excerpt of the executed agreement; clerical or signature errors may be cured by re-execution of corrected signature pages without registry penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online e-service 'Immatriculer une entreprise'; paper counter at Complexe Desjardins, Montréal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite: legal name with S.E.C. suffix; head-office address in Québec; identity and domicile of the general partner; confirmation that one or more limited partners exist (names are not publicly registered under the Bill 54 framework); stated activity NAICS 541810 / ISIC 7310; date of constitution; pay the CAD 80 registration fee and obtain the NEQ (Quebec enterprise number).
required_dossiers: Déclaration d'immatriculation signed by the general partner
Limited partnership agreement kept in the entity file
Proof of head-office address (lease or letter of authorization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of non-conformity, cure the identified defect online within 15 days and re-file the corrected declaration; if rejected, submit a fresh declaration with corrected data and pay any reprocessing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with Revenu Québec and the CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (RQ) one-stop enterprise registration; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business registration for GST/HST and payroll.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NEQ to open the Revenu Québec file; register for Quebec sales tax (QST) and federal GST/HST where taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 threshold; obtain a CRA business number and, if employees are hired, a payroll account; the limited partnership must file annual information returns (e.g., TP-64 for partners) and comply with Canadian-source income allocation rules for non-resident partners.
required_dossiers: Tax identification numbers of all partners
Bank account details for refunds and credits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to RQ or CRA registration query letters by amending the TP-64 or applying for late registration; an assessment or refusal may be objected to within 90 days before the competent tax authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business permit and physical premises clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permits and inspections department (e.g., Ville de Montréal — Permis et inspections); Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for building occupancy; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for occupational health.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the general municipal business permit and occupancy certificate for the head office; verify that the lease is zoned for commercial-office use; ensure compliance with fire and emergency-exit standards; register as an employer with CNESST if staff are hired; no sector-specific provincial license applies to ISIC 7310 media purchasing and affiliate lead generation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is withheld, remedy the fire or structural deficiencies and reapply; an aggrieved applicant may seek municipal administrative review or appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking onboarding, AML/KYC, and enhanced-risk controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or registered financial institution; FINTRAC framework under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open business accounts using the NEQ certificate and the general partner resolution; complete beneficial-ownership KYC forms, noting that non-resident limited partners are permitted; implement an AML/KYC manual commensurate with the 'Medium Risk — Enhanced' rating for affiliate media-buying; configure payment rails (Mercury ACH, wire transfer, Wise) only through the LP's banking and procurement accounts; consult counsel if the activity evolves into a money-services business requiring FINTRAC registration.
required_dossiers: Certified KYC and identity documents for partners
Beneficial ownership register (25% or greater interests)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If onboarding is deferred, provide a sanitized partnership agreement and source-of-funds evidence (affiliate contracts and revenue ledgers); escalate to the financial institution's compliance office; if PCMLTFA triggering criteria appear, file a FINTRAC money-services-business registration before commencing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual updating declaration and registry maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — annual updating declaration (déclaration annuelle de mise à jour).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual updating declaration between January 1 and March 15 each year, confirming the name, head-office address, general partner, and declared activity; pay the annual registry duty based on the revenue band; report any change of partners, general partner, address, or activity within 60 days of the change.
required_dossiers: Access to the REQ dossier using the NEQ
Updated contact information and revenue band
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the enterprise is struck for non-filing, file the late declarations online, pay the compound late penalty, and obtain a reinstated certificate; reinstatement is generally processed within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Direction de l'immatriculation, together with the municipal business-permit department of the head-office city (e.g., Ville de Montréal); no dedicated industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 (digital advertising and media buying).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'immatriculation / Certificate of Registration issued by REQ, supplemented by the municipal business permit (certificat d'occupation / permis d'entreprise) for the head office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category III (low environmental risk for a digital services office); no full EIA report or environmental authorization is required under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process discharges are generated; domestic sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-laws; office HVAC and VOC emissions are minimal and within the thresholds of the Clean Air Regulation (RLRQ, c. Q-2, r. 4.1); electronic waste from media-buying hardware must be managed under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of specific electronic products.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain an occupancy clearance from the local fire safety department in accordance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code (RLRQ, c. B-1.1, r. 0.2). Structural: maintain a building occupancy permit under the Quebec Construction Code (RLRQ, c. B-1.1, r. 0.4) and applicable RBQ standards. Occupational: register with CNESST and implement workplace health and safety plans under the Act respecting Occupational Health and Safety (RLRQ, c. S-2.1, as amended by LQ 2021, c. 27).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal GST/HST and income tax administration; Revenu Québec – Quebec QST and provincial income tax administration. Primary portals: CRA Business Registration Online and My Business Account; Revenu Québec’s Tax Online Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-owned Quebec limited partnership (CA_LP) must first register with the CRA to obtain a federal Business Number (BN) if it carries on business in Canada or makes taxable supplies in Canada; separate GST/HST and payroll accounts are added to the BN as required. The partnership must then register with Revenu Québec to obtain a Quebec Establishment Number (NEQ) and a QST account, or use the integrated Quebec business registration service. Non-resident limited partners without permanent establishment status may require a non-resident tax account, and the partnership must file a T5013 partnership information return to allocate income to the beneficial owners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election. A limited partnership formed in Quebec is fiscally transparent by default under Income Tax Act section 96, provided it qualifies as a Canadian partnership. Partners are taxed directly on allocated partnership income unless a partnership is treated as a corporation under deemed-association rules. Hybrid mismatch and reasonable-allocations rules under sections 18.4, 56.2 and 96(6) apply, and a partnership may file a joint allocation agreement with the CRA; Revenu Québec generally follows the federal allocation and reporting methods.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST registration is mandatory for a person making taxable supplies in Canada in a single calendar quarter or four consecutive calendar quarters exceeding CAD 30,000 in taxable sales. The QST registration threshold is also CAD 30,000 for persons making taxable supplies in Quebec; the threshold applies to a vendor that exceeds it in association with Quebec consumption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time fiscal clearance, e-stamping regime, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing clearance for GST/HST or QST. Standard electronic invoicing is permitted. The CRA and Revenu Québec require that invoices contain prescribed information and be retained in an auditable electronic format. Certain Quebec vendors must register for electronic services through Revenu Québec’s secure portal, but there is no continuous digital fiscal stamping requirement. CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec CléNumérique are used for filings and returns, not for supply-level pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment is available for qualifying supplies under ETA Schedule VI, including tangible personal property exported by the supplier and services supplied to non-residents, such as offshore advertising and affiliate media-buying services, where the service is not received or consumed in Canada by the non-resident client. The Quebec QST zero-rating rules align with the GST framework under Revenu Québec legislation. Eligibility requires the supplier to be registered and the transaction to be supported by contemporaneous documentation that links the supply to a non-resident recipient and to export or offshore delivery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA customs export declaration (B13A or approved reporting equivalent)
Bill of lading / air waybill / other transport evidence for goods
Commercial invoice and advertising services contract
Statement of work / media placement report evidencing offshore recipient
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange settlement record
Proof of payment from the non-resident buyer
T5013 partnership allocation and partner identification records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rated treatment if export documentation is deficient, retroactively assess GST/HST and QST at the full combined rate of 14.975%, and collect interest from the original filing date. False or negligent claims may trigger penalties under the Excise Tax Act including up to CAD 250 plus 5% of gross tax omission or 10% if knowingly made, and willful misstatement can result in higher penalties and prosecution. Revenu Québec may assert equivalent QST clawbacks, impose administrative penalties, and disapply refunds where the FPNR no longer demonstrates real offshore supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential banking supervision and with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF enforcement; Payments Canada operates the national payment clearing and settlement infrastructure (Lynx and Real-Time Rail).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted Article VIII obligations of the IMF Articles of Agreement; the Canadian dollar is fully convertible and Canada maintains no exchange controls on either current-account or capital-account transactions. A Quebec limited partnership may remit operational profits to non-resident limited partners without prior approval from the Bank of Canada or the Department of Finance, at freely floating market rates. The civil-law framework of Quebec imposes no capital controls on the CA_LP, and partner capital withdrawals, loan interest, management fees, and profit distributions are freely repatriable once applicable Canadian income tax compliance is discharged: non-resident partners are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada) on their allocated share of the LP's Canadian-source income under the flow-through mechanics of section 96 and may claim treaty relief where available; no Part XIII withholding attaches to the distribution of already-taxed partnership income. Practical friction is exclusively bank-driven—sanctions screening, beneficial ownership verification, and source-of-funds documentation—and does not arise from currency regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory deadline for repatriating export receipts. The CA_LP may retain USD and other foreign-currency receipts indefinitely, whether in foreign-currency accounts at Canadian chartered banks or in offshore accounts. No Bank of Canada filing accompanies receipt of the funds; the only recurring obligations are (i) balance-of-payments statistical reporting of cross-border service exports through the Bank of Canada / Statistics Canada International Transactions Reporting System (bank-facilitated), (ii) filing of the federal T5013 partnership information return and the corresponding Quebec provincial partnership declaration with Revenu Québec, and (iii) FINTRAC's reporting duty for single or linked large transactions equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000, including large virtual-currency transactions, within 24 hours. There is no requirement to convert USD into CAD before settling Canadian-dollar liabilities; the partnership may naturally hedge by maintaining both currency legs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Treasury Account (CAD and USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Corporate Account / USD Clearing via RBC Bank (US correspondent)
Operational CAD Account / USD Settlement via BMO Harris Bank
Operational Account / Global Trade and FX Services
Operational Account / Global Transaction Banking and Cross-Border Corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM–HIGH as a secondary disbursement rail; LOW as a primary settlement bank. Wise (TransferWise) can onboard a Quebec-registered limited partnership and provides multi-currency routing through a FINTRAC-registered Canadian money services business operating under sponsorship of regulated banks; it is acceptable for low-value publisher and sub-affiliate payouts but not for the capital escrow relationship. Mercury (US) does not accept Canadian legal entities without substantive US operations and is therefore not viable. EU-passported electronic money institutions (e.g., Airwallex) cannot book a Quebec LP account directly without obtaining a Canadian MSB registration or operating through an authorized foreign bank branch; indirect sponsorship creates correspondent and enhanced due diligence complexity. The recommended treasury architecture is a Canadian Schedule I bank as the sole primary settlement member and Payments Canada participant, with fintechs capped to small-value bulk disbursement rails—for example, less than CAD 5,000 per beneficiary per day—to minimize correspondent risk and keep AML/KYC fully layered.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated for at least one authorised signatory and the AML/compliance principal of the CA_LP at initial onboarding in Quebec. Remote-only opening is not offered by Schedule I banks for a limited partnership whose general partner is a corporation with non-resident limited partners; the enhanced due diligence overlay (FINTRAC PCMLTFA obligations and perceived ad-tech fraud/chargeback risk) triggers an in-branch interview at a Montreal business banking centre, supplemented by a video-verified interview for additional signatories. The bank will require original or notarized copies of the partnership declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (no older than three months), the executed partnership agreement, corporate resolutions of the general partner appointing signatories, personal identification and proof of address for every natural-person ultimate beneficial owner, and, where the general partner is a corporation, its certificate of good standing. RBC and National Bank permit a hybrid model (one in-person meeting plus remote attestation for the remaining directors); TD and CIBC reserve the right to require all directors of the general partner to appear physically.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque chain of control: a corporate general partner with directors resident outside Quebec or in mixed high-risk and low-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement and certificate of registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; general partner certificate of corporate status issued within 30 days; notarized beneficial ownership attestation identifying all individuals exercising 25% or greater control; full organizational chart of the ultimate beneficial ownership stack; passport copies and recent proof of address for each individual; corporate register excerpt listing directors and registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners, or a limited partner structured as a trust or foreign holding vehicle, that impair sanctions screening or source-of-wealth verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO chain traced to natural persons with government-issued identification; executed subscription documents and capital commitment schedules; FATCA/CRS self-certifications (US W-8BEN-E or equivalent CRS forms) for each non-resident limited partner; source-of-funds evidence comprising bank statements, sale or closing statements, or audited financial statements of the contributor; OFAC, UN, EU, and Canadian Special Economic Measures Act sanctions screening output for every limited partner; letters from each contributor's regulated banking institution confirming the provenance of contributed funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ad-tech / performance-media-buying model (NAICS 541810 / ISIC 7310) flagged for third-party payment processor abuse, mule accounts, and chargeback risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business-model white paper describing the media arbitrage flow; executed insertion orders and performance contracts with each advertiser (Google Ads, Meta, native and push networks); platform billing dashboards and publisher settlement statements; three-way reconciliation files linking advertiser invoices, CA_LP ledger entries, and publisher payouts; complete sub-affiliate list with KYC; invoice register; AML/ATF compliance program adopted under the PCMLTFA; appointment of an AML compliance officer; anti-fraud and chargeback-response policy; 12-month historical transaction records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-velocity cross-border flows (weekly USD receipts and distributed publisher payouts to more than 20 countries) triggering enhanced due diligence on the partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prior-year reviewed or audited financial statements; 12-month treasury forecast with projected settlement volumes; narrative explanation of ad-spend cycles and publisher payment terms; 12-month counterparty breakdown by country; corporate resolutions authorising transaction limits and signatory mandates; KYC files for all material payees and supply-side vendors; signed undertaking to adopt daily velocity caps, sub-limits, and dual-approval controls; confirmations of current balance-of-payments statistical reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Co-mingling exposure arising from a request to maintain USD and CAD accounts alongside parent or sister entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany agreements (cost-sharing, marketing services, or administrative services agreements); transfer pricing documentation consistent with the OECD arm's-length standard; segregated ledger policies and account-designation letters issued by the general partner; intercompany settlement schedule with monthly netting statement; independent accountant's letter confirming segregation of the LP's funds from affiliate entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident limited partners remit capital by SWIFT MT103 to the CA_LP's Capital Escrow Account at its primary Schedule I bank in Montreal, using a payment narrative substantially in the form of 'Capital subscription – Quebec société en commandite, declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec' and, for Bank of Canada / Statistics Canada balance-of-payments purposes, the IMF BPM6 category 'direct investment in Canada – equity injection into a Canadian partnership' as transmitted by the receiving bank. Pre-crediting controls include: (i) confirmation that the remitter name matches the subscription schedules of the partnership agreement; (ii) clearance of OFAC, UN, EU, and Canadian SEMA sanctions screening on the remitter and all ultimate principals; (iii) completion of source-of-wealth and UBO dossiers; and (iv) verification that the funds are not third-party pass-through payments. On clearance, CAD is journaled from the Capital Escrow Account to the Operational Account via internal treasury transfer with no FX conversion; USD receipts are parked in a USD sub-account and converted only at treasury direction through the bank's FX desk, never automatically at spot. Non-resident limited partners whose aggregate injections meet or exceed the statutory threshold must file the prescribed notification under the Investment Canada Act, although a passive limited-partner interest in a media-buying partnership below the review threshold normally receives notification-only clearance. Contributions are recorded as contributed capital for Part I tax purposes and are excluded from the LP's annual income allocation on the T5013 and Quebec partnership declarations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of media-buying disbursements to advertisers, publisher networks, data partners, and sub-affiliates is executed through differentiated clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for all cross-border USD wires, with US clearing via Fedwire/CHIPS through the bank's US correspondent (RBC Bank for RBC, BMO Harris for BMO, and comparable correspondents for other banks); (2) US ACH credits for recurring sub-threshold disbursements to US publishers and affiliates through the bank's US-domiciled deposit network; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit, structurally permissible but deployed only for large committed annual ad-spend contracts where the media owner requires proof of funds; (4) Canadian domestic CAD settlement through Payments Canada's Lynx high-value system and Real-Time Rail for instant sub-threshold payments, supplemented by Interac e-Transfer for micro-disbursements below CAD 1,000. Every outbound remittance references the underlying invoice, insertion order, or publisher contract and carries a service-export purpose narrative consistent with the BPM6 category 'advertising and market research services' to suppress the third-party money-mule red flag. The treasury function applies a 95/5 conversion rule: 95% of forecast USD receipts are covered by forward contracts, and the residual 5% is retained unhedged to absorb variable publisher payout spikes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD over-the-counter FX forwards (one to twelve-month tenors) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with an OSFI-regulated investment dealer, exempt from mandatory clearing as bona fide trade-hedging transactions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) – legally permissible as OTC derivatives under Canadian securities laws and the Quebec Derivatives Act, but commercially redundant for CAD given full deliverability of the currency
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD basis swaps) for tenor-matched hedging of long-dated capital exposures, supported by a Credit Support Annex collateral arrangement
CAD/USD vanilla FX options, collars, and participating forward structures purchased from banks or investment dealers for asymmetric protection on media-buying margin
Average-rate (Asian) FX forwards providing rolling monthly hedging of recurring USD advertising receipts to smooth conversion rates across publisher payout cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the registration anniversary date (e.g., June 15 registration ⇒ due August 14 annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing tariff surcharge; statutory fines up to CAD 5,000 for a natural person and CAD 15,000 for a legal entity; administrative strike-off of the enterprise after continuous one-year non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership fiscal period end (calendar December 31 year-end ⇒ due June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day per partner up to 100 days, with a CAD 100 minimum; partners' allocated losses may be disallowed under Income Tax Act subsection 162(6)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after fiscal year-end for partnerships carrying on business in Quebec (December 31 year-end ⇒ due June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of CAD 25 per day per partner up to 100 days; interest on unreported balances; parallel provincial administrative and evidentiary exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Persons with Significant Control (UBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – integrated into Annual Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days of registration anniversary; any unit transfer conferring 25% or more effective control must be reported to the REQ within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offences under CQLR c P-44.1 ss. 50.16–50.17: fines up to CAD 5,000 for individuals and CAD 15,000 for legal persons; directors of the general partner may be personally liable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST and QST Return (elected annual remitter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST) and Revenu Québec (QST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after fiscal year-end (calendar year-end ⇒ due March 31); payment due at the same deadline for eligible annual remitters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance due, plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months); interest at prescribed CRA and Revenu Québec rates

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec société en commandite (LP) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; the QBCA compulsory-audit regime applies only to the general partner corporation and may be waived by unanimous shareholder consent for a non-reporting issuer with fewer than 15 shareholders; an independent audit may be contractually required by the LP agreement, limited partner rights, or CRA/Revenu Québec audit demand in high-risk cross-border media-buying scenarios
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) is the default framework for private Quebec LPs; IFRS applies only to publicly accountable entities or if the LP agreement affirmatively elects it; T5013 and CO-17 schedules are prepared on the tax basis of accounting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LP must maintain the Quebec Register of Individuals with Significant Control (Registre des personnes ayant un contrôle significatif). Any unit transfer or change in control reaching 25% or more of partnership units must be recorded in the register within 15 days and notified to the REQ within 30 days; the annual declaration reconfirms the UBO listing as of the anniversary date; failure to update invalidates the new transferee partner's ability to rely on pass-through allocation evidence
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)
Minute Book and Resolutions Register (General Partner and partnership level)
Accounting Records and Supporting T5013/CO-17 Schedules

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 – USD 1,100 (CAD 300–1,500) typical annual market range for a registered office/agent in Montreal or Quebec City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 18,000 (CAD 7,000–25,000) for a private affiliate media-buying LP, depending on transaction volume and cross-border payout complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% general corporate rate; note: Limited Partnership is a pass-through entity, partners taxed at their own rates)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% and Quebec rate to 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs); SR&ED tax credits; Quebec tax credits for production and innovation; not directly applicable to LP but partners may claim flow-through incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal) filed via CRA My Business Account or authorized E-file; Quebec Relevé 15 (RL-15) and provincial partnership return (CO-17) via Revenu Québec's online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; Quebec CO-17 due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (same deadline).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership identification: legal name, business number, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Canadian business number (BN) and ensure non-resident partners are identified with their country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income/loss to each partner (proportionate share).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report each non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source income; attach Schedule 50 for non-resident partner details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue and expenses (including advertising costs, media buying, and operating expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure expenses are arm's length and supported by TP documentation if cross-border transactions exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-specific income allocation and provincial tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must file Quebec income tax return if they have Quebec-source income; RL-15 must be filed with Revenu Québec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax payable (if any) plus 1% per month up to 12 months; for information returns, penalties range from CAD 25 to CAD 100 per day for each partner, up to CAD 2,500 per partner; Quebec penalties similar under Taxation Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid to non-residents under domestic law (Part XIII of Income Tax Act); reduced to 5% under Canada-US treaty for portfolio dividends, 15% for substantial holdings; for LP distributions, character of income (e.g., business income, interest, royalties) determines WHT, not dividend rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident partner must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR301) to the partnership or payer; partnership must file Form NR301 with CRA to reduce withholding; for Quebec, additional provincial relief may require Form TP-1016. The TRC must be issued by the foreign tax authority and submitted before payment or within a reasonable time to claim refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% (Part XIII), treaty reduced to 10% (US) or 0% for certain IP under Canada-US treaty; interest: statutory 25%, treaty reduced to 15% (US) or 0% for arm's length interest; Quebec does not impose separate WHT on interest/royalties to non-residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for goods transactions and CAD 500,000 for services/intangibles with non-residents (per CRA TP documentation thresholds); Master File required if total gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million and cross-border transactions exceed CAD 5 million; Local File required if transactions exceed CAD 1 million (goods) or CAD 500,000 (services).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Section 245 of the Income Tax Act can recharacterize transactions lacking economic substance; for LPs, CRA may scrutinize whether the partnership has real business purpose and substance (e.g., office, employees, decision-making in Canada) to avoid treaty shopping or sham arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of cross-border transactions (e.g., underreporting media buying revenue, inflating expenses).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act Section 239: fine of 50% to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 50% of understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of corporate partners may be personally liable for unpaid taxes under Section 227.1 (director's liability) if they fail to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset freezes possible under tax evasion investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: LP established solely to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions without real business operations, employees, or decision-making in Canada; artificial intercompany transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization: denial of tax benefits, reassessment of income, interest and penalties up to 50% of tax avoided; potential treaty override.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for negligence if they approved sham transactions; CRA can impose director's liability for penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) if handling large volumes of digital payments; failure to implement AML/KYC procedures for affiliate partners or media vendors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA): fines up to CAD 1 million for individuals, CAD 2 million for entities; criminal charges for money laundering under Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined or imprisoned (up to 5 years) for knowingly failing to comply with AML obligations; regulatory bans on operating financial services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing in cross-border media buying transactions with related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can adjust income, impose penalties of 10% of net adjustment (if documentation incomplete), plus interest; double taxation risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in TP mispricing; CRA can pursue director liability for unpaid corporate taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing T5013 or Quebec CO-17 filing deadlines, or failing to provide partner information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax payable (if any) plus 1% per month up to 12 months; for information returns, penalties per partner per day (CAD 25-100) up to CAD 2,500 per partner; Quebec similar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they were responsible for filing and failed to do so; CRA can assess director liability.
